name: – Motion for a resolution
title: Resolution on the draft Commission regulation amending Annexes II and III to Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards maximum residue levels for cyproconazole and spirodiclofen in or on certain products
part_text:
The European Parliament is against a draft European Commission rule on pesticide leftovers in food. The rule would keep allowed levels of cyproconazole, a banned pesticide, on many imported foods such as cereals, coffee, sugar beet and meat. Parliament says this is unsafe and gives farmers outside the EU an unfair advantage. It asks the Commission to withdraw the rule and propose new limits of 0.01 mg/kg for all products.

- The rule would keep cyproconazole residues allowed on many imported foods; Parliament rejects it.
- It affects EU farmers, consumers, and food importers from outside the EU.
- Parliament asks the Commission to withdraw the draft and propose stricter limits.
